root_causes.description: The product-catalog pod was killed and rescheduled during the window (Kubernetes events show 'Killing: Stopping container product-catalog' and 'SuccessfulDelete: Deleted pod: product-catalog-5bb7676754-hcfpv', followed by Scheduling/Pulling/Created/Started of replacement pod product-catalog-64896fcd4f-jzqxs). Because product-catalog is the heavily-depended-on leaf (frontend, checkout, recommendation all call it), its crash/restart stalls the whole call graph and produces the observed telemetry blackout (all server request/error rates flat at 0).

evidence.expected_baseline: no container kill/stop events for a steady-state service
pod not deleted during steady state

evidence.observed_value: new pod product-catalog-64896fcd4f-jzqxs scheduled and started after the kill
evidence.expected_baseline: no pod rescheduling during steady state
product-catalog should serve non-zero server request rate

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.001 cores (near-idle, far below the ~2.1 core saturation seen in the prior cpu_stress incident)
evidence.expected_baseline: product-catalog serving traffic would show measurable CPU above idle

root_causes.description: Traces involving product-catalog are present but extremely slow (search_traces p95_duration=13818ms; individual spans 3111ms/5000ms/6889ms) with zero errors, indicating severe latency/stall rather than outright request failure — consistent with a restarting/stalled pod whose requests queue behind the outage.

evidence.expected_baseline: product-catalog p95 well under 1000ms in steady state
p95 latency in the low-hundreds of ms

root_causes.description: Frontend server request rate is flat at 0 and its traces show inflated latency (p95 15001ms) with no errors, the classic propagation signature of an upstream dependency (product-catalog) stalling. Ranked lower because frontend shows no independent resource or crash anomaly (CPU 0.293 mean, normal).

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend should serve non-zero server request rate
frontend CPU with active load ~0.3 cores

remediation_steps: Confirm current product-catalog pod health: kubectl get pods -n otel-demo -l app.kubernetes.io/name=product-catalog and kubectl describe pod product-catalog-64896fcd4f-jzqxs to inspect restart/termination reasons.
Inspect why the pod was deleted (Killing/Stopping container) and whether a chaos/pod-kill fault or OOM/probe failure is involved; stop any injected pod-kill fault if present.
Verify the OTel Collector / telemetry pipeline (otel-collector pod and exporter connectivity) since server request/error rates are flat at 0 across all services.
After product-catalog stabilizes, re-check request/error rates and trace latency for product-catalog, frontend, checkout and recommendation to confirm recovery.
Add/verify PodDisruptionBudget, readiness/liveness probe tuning and replica count so a single product-catalog pod restart does not stall the whole call graph.
